name: Weaver Loop Runners
title: Weaver Loop Runners: Light-Duty Webbing Slings
meta: Weaver loop runners are sewn webbing loops for light rigging, gear anchors, and redirects. How to hitch them, where they fit, and how to inspect the webbing.
tagline: Sewn webbing loops for light rigging points, redirects, and gear anchors.
summary: Weaver loop runners are sewn, endless webbing slings for light-duty work: hanging a small block, setting a redirect, or girth-hitching an anchor for gear. They pack small, cost little, and cover a lot of the odd jobs a crew runs into on a pruning or light removal day.
highlights: Sewn endless loop of flat webbing
Girth, choke, or basket around a limb
Light and compact on the saddle or in the bag
Handy for redirects and small rigging points
Inexpensive enough to keep several lengths
specs: Marked on the sling; varies by length and width

body.h: Where loop runners earn their place
p: A loop runner is the sling you grab when the job is small. Girth-hitch one around a limb to hang a light pulley for a lowering line on pruning cuts, or to set a quick redirect that keeps your rope out of a crotch. On the ground it works as a temporary anchor around a stem or a truck hitch point for a tag line.

Because they are flat webbing, runners sit close to the bark and are easy to untie and pull down. Keep a couple of lengths in the rigging bag so you are not tying up a long rope sling for a two-minute task. Browse the rest of our rigging slings when the load gets heavier.

Light-duty means light-duty. Webbing runners are not a substitute for a rated rope sling or round sling under a shock-loaded rigging block, and a choked or girth-hitched sling holds less than one pulled straight. Read the marking and size the sling for the real load.

Before each use, check for cuts, abrasion, glazing from heat, chemical stains, and broken stitching at the sewn joint. Keep runners away from the saw and sharp edges. If a runner is ever used as part of a climbing system, life-support use must follow ANSI Z133, the manufacturer's instructions, and your training.

faq.q: Can I use a Weaver loop runner for rigging logs?
faq.a: Only small, controlled pieces within its marked rating. For blocking down wood or any shock load, use a rope or round sling sized for the job.

faq.q: How should I attach a loop runner to a limb?
faq.a: A girth hitch or a basket around the limb is common. Remember that a girth or choke hitch reduces the sling's capacity compared with a straight pull.

name: CMI RNA Pulley
title: CMI RNA Pulley: Micro Pulley for Climbing Systems
meta: The CMI RNA pulley is a compact micro pulley for hitch tending and small haul systems. Where it fits in a climbing setup, what to check, and how to care for it.
tagline: A compact CMI micro pulley for hitch tending and small rope systems.
summary: The CMI RNA pulley is a small, light micro pulley built for rope access style systems, and tree climbers use it as a hitch tender and in small mechanical advantage setups. It clips onto a carabiner below your friction hitch and keeps slack moving through as you climb.
highlights: Tends a friction hitch so slack feeds smoothly
Useful for small haul and redirect setups
Light enough to live on the saddle
Made by an established US rope-hardware maker
specs: Hitch tending, small haul systems, redirects

body.h: How climbers use a micro pulley
p: On a moving rope system the most common job for a micro pulley is tending the hitch. The pulley rides on the bridge carabiner below a Distel or VT, and as you pull slack up through the system the sheave pushes the hitch up the rope. It saves you reaching down to advance the knot on every pull and makes footlocking or body-thrusting smoother.
The same pulley earns its keep off the saddle too: a small redirect, a pulley on a tag line, or the moving pulley in a light-duty haul. See our other micro pulleys to compare size and weight.

Check the side-plate marking for the rope diameter range and rated strength, and make sure your hitch cord and climbing line fall inside it. A rope that is too big for the sheave rubs the side plates and loses efficiency.

Before each climb, spin the sheave and listen for grinding, look for grooves worn into the sheave or plates, and check that the side plates close fully on the axle. Keep it clean of sap and grit. Any pulley in your life-support system has to be inspected before use, and life-support use must follow ANSI Z133, the manufacturer's instructions, and your training.

faq.q: Is a micro pulley required for hitch climbing?
faq.a: No, but most climbers use one. It tends the hitch so you do not have to push it up the rope by hand, which makes advancing faster and smoother.

faq.q: Will the CMI RNA pulley work with my hitch cord?
faq.a: Check the rope range on the side plate against your hitch cord and climbing line diameter before you put it into service.

name: Notch RC Grapple
title: Notch RC Grapple: Line Retrieval Hook for Arborists
meta: The Notch RC Grapple is a small grapple for snagging and retrieving lines, lanyards, and hung gear in the canopy. How crews use it and what to watch for.
tagline: A small grapple for snagging stuck lines and hung gear out of the canopy.
summary: The Notch RC Grapple is a compact retrieval grapple that tree crews use to snag a stuck throw line, a dropped lanyard tail, or a rope that will not come back down. Tie it to a light line, toss or lower it, and hook what you need instead of sending a climber up for it.
highlights: Compact grapple for retrieving lines and gear
Ties to throw line or light cord
Saves a climb to fetch a hung line
Small enough to keep in the throw-line bag
From Notch, a long-time arborist gear brand
specs: Snagging and retrieving lines and gear
Life support or anchoring a climber

p: Every crew has watched a throw line wrap itself around a stub, or a rope tail drape over a limb just out of reach. A small grapple tied to a length of throw line lets you go after it from the ground or from your position in the tree. Swing or toss the grapple past the stuck line, let it settle, and pull back slowly so the tines catch.
It also helps when you are retrieving a false crotch setup or pulling a tag line back across a gap. Keep it in the throw-line bag with your other climbing extras so it is there when you need it.

A grapple is a retrieval tool only. Never use it as an anchor, never clip it into a climbing or rigging system, and never put a person's weight on it. Make sure the drop zone is clear before you throw, because a grapple that pulls free comes back down hard.

Pull steadily rather than yanking, so you do not snap a limb or set the hooks into something you cannot release. Check the tines and the tie-in point for bending or cracks, and replace the cord you tie it to when it gets worn.

faq.q: Can I anchor a rope with the Notch RC Grapple?
faq.a: No. It is a retrieval tool for snagging lines and gear and must never be used for climbing, rigging, or any load-bearing anchor.

faq.q: What line should I tie the grapple to?
faq.a: A spare throw line or light cord works well. Use something you can afford to cut away if the grapple gets stuck.

name: Husqvarna 545 Mark II / 550 XP Mark II Tune-Up Kit
title: Husqvarna 550 XP Mark II Tune-Up Kit (Also 545 II)
h1: Husqvarna 545 Mark II / 550 XP Mark II Tune-Up Kit
meta: A Husqvarna 550 XP Mark II tune-up kit that also fits the 545 Mark II. What a tune-up covers, when to do it, and how it keeps a ground saw cutting hard.
tagline: Service parts for a routine tune-up on the 545 Mark II and 550 XP Mark II saws.
summary: A Husqvarna 550 XP Mark II tune-up kit puts the common wear parts for a routine service in one package, and it fits the 545 Mark II as well. It is the easy way to bring a hard-working ground saw back to clean starts and full power after a season of bucking and limbing.
highlights: Matched to the 545 Mark II and 550 XP Mark II
Groups routine wear parts in one order
Restores easy starting and clean running
Good annual or seasonal service item
Keeps a spare on the truck for the busy months
specs: Husqvarna 545 Mark II, 550 XP Mark II
Check the listing for the exact parts included

body.h: Why tune up a ground saw
p: The 545 Mark II and 550 XP Mark II are workhorse 50cc-class saws for limbing, bucking, and small felling. They run on AutoTune, which adjusts the mixture on its own, but it can only work with what it is given. A choked air filter, a tired spark plug, or a dirty fuel filter will still cost you power and make the saw hard to start.

Replacing those wear parts together is quick and cheap compared with the downtime of a saw that will not start at the chipper. Many crews do it at the start of the season and again whenever a saw has been run hard in dusty wood. Find more service parts in our power equipment parts section.

Work on a cool saw with the switch off and the chain brake on. Clean around the covers before you open them so grit does not fall into the intake. Fit new parts as the operator's manual describes, gap and torque the plug to spec, and use fresh, correctly mixed fuel afterward.
Compare the kit contents with your saw's parts list before you start, and if the saw still runs poorly after a tune-up, have a dealer check it rather than chasing settings yourself.

faq.q: Does this kit fit the 545 Mark II and the 550 XP Mark II?
faq.a: Yes, it is listed for both. Always confirm the parts against your saw's manual or model plate before installing.

faq.q: How often should I tune up my 550 XP Mark II?
faq.a: Follow the manual's maintenance schedule. Most working crews clean the air filter often and replace the wear parts at least once a season.

name: Husqvarna Drive Belt for K770 Cut-Off Saw
title: Husqvarna K770 Belt: Replacement Cut-Off Saw Drive Belt
h1: Husqvarna K770 Belt for Cut-Off Saw
meta: Replacement Husqvarna K770 belt for the K770 power cutter. Signs a drive belt is worn, how to fit and tension it, and why to keep a spare in the truck box.
tagline: A replacement drive belt to keep a Husqvarna K770 power cutter on the job.
summary: The Husqvarna K770 belt is the replacement drive belt for the K770 cut-off saw, the power cutter many crews carry for cutting cable, bolts, and hardware on removals and storm work. A worn belt slips and stalls the blade, so a spare in the truck box keeps the saw working.
highlights: Replacement drive belt for the K770
Restores full blade speed under load
Small, cheap spare that prevents downtime
Swap in the field with basic tools
Genuine fit for the cutting arm

p: A power cutter's belt does a lot of work. Signs it is due: the blade slows or stops in the cut while the engine keeps revving, you smell hot rubber, or you can see cracks, glazing, fraying, or missing ribs on the belt. Running a slipping belt only builds heat and wears the pulleys.

On tree jobs the K770 tends to come out for cutting old cable-and-bracing hardware, embedded bolts, or chain, so it may sit for weeks between uses. Check the belt before you need it, not when you are standing at the stump. More replacement parts are in our power equipment parts section.

With the engine off and the blade removed or guarded, remove the belt guard, release the tension, and slip the old belt off. Fit the new belt, set tension as the operator's manual describes, and refit the guard before you start the saw.

Run the saw briefly, then recheck tension, because a new belt seats in. Wear eye, hearing, and respiratory protection when cutting, and keep the blade guard set to throw sparks and debris away from you and the crew.
Store the spare belt flat in its packaging, out of sun and away from fuel, so it is in good shape when you finally need it.

faq.q: Will this belt fit other Husqvarna cut-off saws?
faq.a: It is listed for the K770. For other models, check the parts list for your saw before ordering.

faq.q: Why does my K770 blade stop while the engine still runs?
faq.a: A slipping or loose belt is the most common cause. Check tension and belt condition first.

name: 9/16" Ship Auger Bit
title: 9/16 Ship Auger Bit for Tree Cabling and Bracing
meta: A 9/16 ship auger bit for drilling clean through-holes for cabling and bracing hardware. Why a ship auger suits green wood, sizing tips, and drilling advice.
tagline: A long ship auger bit for drilling clean holes for tree cabling hardware.
summary: A 9/16 ship auger bit is the drill bit arborists reach for when installing cabling and bracing hardware, because its single spur and open flute clear green, wet wood without binding. The 9/16 inch size is a common match for 1/2 inch threaded rod and eye bolts.
highlights: 9/16 inch diameter for 1/2 inch rod hardware
specs: 1/2 in threaded rod and eye bolts

body.h: Why a ship auger for tree work
p: Green wood is wet, stringy, and heavy, and standard twist bits pack up and bind. A ship auger has a single cutting spur and a wide, open flute that lifts chips out of a deep hole, so you can drill through a stem for a through-bolt or a dynamic anchor without constantly backing out.

Sizing the bit just over the rod diameter, such as 9/16 inch for 1/2 inch rod, gives a snug fit that still lets the hardware go in without forcing it. Check the hardware maker's instructions for the hole size they specify. Our cabling and bracing section has the rod, eyes, and cable to go with it.

Use a powerful drill with a side handle and a slow speed, and keep the bit straight so the hole lines up from one side of the stem to the other. Back out every so often to clear chips. Drilling aloft means managing torque on a lanyard, so set your position well and keep both hands on the drill.
Keep the cutting spur sharp and dry the bit after use so it does not rust. Cabling and bracing should be planned and installed by trained arborists following ANSI A300 and Z133 practice.

faq.q: What size hardware does a 9/16 bit match?
faq.a: It is commonly used for 1/2 inch threaded rod and eye bolts. Always confirm the hole size the hardware maker specifies.

faq.q: Why not use a spade bit or twist bit?
faq.a: In wet, green wood they tend to clog and bind. A ship auger clears chips better on deep through-holes.

name: Rigguy Wire Stops
title: Rigguy Wire Stops for Tree Cabling and Guying
meta: Rigguy wire stops terminate wire rope or strand without bulky clamps, for tree cabling and guying. Sizing, installation basics, and inspection for arborists.
tagline: Compact wire terminations for tree cabling and guying work.
summary: Rigguy wire stops are compact terminations that hold the end of wire rope or strand, used by arborists for cabling, guying, and tree support systems. They replace stacks of wire rope clips on some installs, which makes for a neater, faster job in the canopy.
highlights: Clean, compact look in the tree
Sized to match a specific wire diameter
specs: Match the stop to your wire diameter

p: Steel cabling systems and tree guying both need a reliable way to end the wire. Traditional methods use thimbles and wire rope clips or preformed dead-ends. A wire stop is a compact alternative on some systems: the wire passes through the anchor hole or hardware and the stop holds it on the far side.
The result is a tidy install with fewer parts hanging in the canopy, and less time aloft with a wrench. Look through our cabling hardware for compatible wire and anchors.

Fewer parts also means fewer places for a mistake. With clips, every saddle has to be on the live side and every nut torqued; with a stop sized correctly, the termination is a single, consistent piece that is easy to check from a distance on later inspections.

A wire stop only works on the wire size it is made for, so match it exactly to your cable or strand diameter and follow the maker's instructions for installation, hole size, and load use. Do not mix brands or improvise with a stop that is close to the right size.

Cabling systems should be designed and installed to ANSI A300 by trained arborists and inspected on a regular schedule. At each check, look for wire slipping, corrosion, broken strands, and bark growing over the hardware. Wire stops are tree-support hardware, not climbing or rigging gear.

faq.q: Can I use Rigguy wire stops for lifting or rigging?
faq.a: No. Use them for the cabling or guying applications the maker lists, not for rigging, lifting, or life support.

faq.q: How do I pick the right size?
faq.a: Match the stop to the exact diameter of your wire or strand and follow the maker's sizing chart.

name: SMC Apex 1.1 Pulley
title: SMC Apex 1.1 Pulley for Arborist Rigging Systems
meta: The SMC Apex 1.1 pulley is a compact, rescue-grade pulley for redirects, haul systems, and light rigging. How tree crews use it and how to inspect it.
tagline: A compact rescue-grade pulley for redirects, haul systems, and light rigging.
summary: The SMC Apex 1.1 pulley is a compact pulley from a well-known rescue hardware maker, and tree crews use it for redirects, mechanical advantage systems, and light rigging. It is small enough to carry on the saddle but built for real rope work.
highlights: Good for redirects and haul systems
Fits on a standard locking carabiner

body.h: Using a compact pulley on tree jobs
p: A small, strong pulley is one of the most useful pieces in the rigging bag. Use it as a redirect to change the direction of a pull, as the moving pulley in a 3:1 for tensioning a line, or to take friction out of a tag line that has to run around a stem.
For climbers it can work in a pulley-saver setup or as part of a haul system to lift a saw or a heavier tool. Compare sizes and styles in our rigging pulleys before you choose.
Compared with running rope over a carabiner, a pulley cuts friction and rope wear considerably, which you notice on every pull of a haul system and in the life of your tag lines.

Check the markings for the rope diameter range and rated strength, and keep loads well inside them. A compact pulley is not a rigging block for blocking down big wood; shock loads belong on a block built for them.

Before each use, spin the sheave, open and close the side plates, and look for cracks, sharp edges, grooves, or a wobbling axle. Clean off sap and grit. If the pulley ever goes into a life-support system, life-support use must follow ANSI Z133, the manufacturer's instructions, and your training.

faq.q: Can I use the SMC Apex pulley for blocking down wood?
faq.a: Not for heavy or shock-loaded rigging. Use a rigging block rated for the job and keep compact pulleys for redirects and haul systems.

faq.q: What rope size does it take?
faq.a: Read the rope range marked on the side plate and match it to your line before use.

name: SMC Apex Direct 1.1 Pulley
title: SMC Apex Direct 1.1 Pulley for Rigging and Haul Systems
meta: The SMC Apex Direct 1.1 pulley is a compact, rescue-grade pulley for redirects and haul systems on tree jobs. Where it fits, what to check, and care tips.
tagline: A compact SMC pulley in the Apex Direct style for redirects and haul systems.
summary: The SMC Apex Direct 1.1 pulley is a compact, rescue-grade pulley that tree crews use for redirects, haul systems, and light rigging. It sits in the same family as the standard Apex, so check the configuration against how you plan to clip it into your system.
highlights: Compact SMC pulley, Apex Direct style
Redirects, haul systems, and light rigging

body.h: What it does on the job
p: On a tree crew a small pulley gets used constantly: redirecting a lowering line around a stem, building a 3:1 to tension a tag line, or hauling a saw up to the climber. A compact rescue-style pulley handles these tasks with less friction than a carabiner and less weight than a full rigging block.
Before buying, compare the Apex Direct with the standard Apex and other options in our rigging pulleys so the attachment style suits the way you rig.

A pulley that lives on the saddle or in the rigging bag gets used far more than one left in the truck. Its small size means you can carry it all day and reach for it whenever a rope is rubbing over a limb or a pull needs a cleaner angle.
Keep loads inside the marked rating and use rope within the marked diameter range. Do not use a compact pulley as a block for blocking down heavy wood.

Check the sheave for smooth spin, the side plates for cracks or burrs, and the axle for play before each use. Wash out sap and grit and let it dry. If it goes into a climbing or rescue system, life-support use must follow ANSI Z133, the manufacturer's instructions, and your training.
Store it dry and away from chemicals, and keep track of its history. A pulley that has been dropped from height onto rock or concrete should be retired unless the maker says otherwise.

faq.q: What is the difference between the Apex and the Apex Direct?
faq.a: They are related compact pulleys with different configurations. Check the maker's details to see which suits the way you connect it.

faq.q: Is it rated for life support?
faq.a: Check the markings and maker's documentation. Use any life-support gear only as the manufacturer and ANSI Z133 allow.

name: 3/4" Mammoth Rigging Line
title: 3/4 Mammoth Rigging Line for Heavy Tree Rigging
meta: A 3/4 Mammoth rigging line for heavy blocking, big negative rigging, and removals. Why crews choose 3/4 inch rope, how to match hardware, and how to inspect it.
tagline: A 3/4 inch rigging line for heavy blocking and big removal work.
summary: The 3/4 Mammoth rigging line is a heavy-duty rope for big removal work, where crews block down large wood and need a line with plenty of strength and abrasion resistance. At 3/4 inch it runs through full-size rigging blocks and lowering devices built for heavy rigging.
highlights: Made for blocking down large wood
Matches full-size blocks and lowering devices
Good grip in the hand on the ground
Choose length to suit your tallest trees
specs: See the maker's rated breaking strength

p: Most crews run 1/2 or 5/8 inch rope for everyday rigging, then step up to 3/4 inch when the wood gets big. Heavy tops, long leaders, and large blocked-down rounds all generate shock loads that a thicker line handles with more margin and less stretch-related surprise.

The tradeoff is weight and bulk. A 3/4 inch line is heavier to carry, takes more room in the bag, and needs a block and lowering device rated for that diameter. Compare it with other lines in our rigging rope before you commit.
Choose the length by the tallest trees you rig. You need enough rope to reach from the ground to the rigging point and back down to the lowering device with a few wraps and some tail to spare.

Match every piece of the system to the rope: block sheave, porta-wrap or bollard, slings, and knots all affect working strength. Use the maker's rated breaking strength, apply a sensible working load limit, and remember that knots and sharp bends reduce strength.

Inspect the line before every job for cut or pulled strands, glazed or melted sections, flat spots, and core damage. Retire rope that has been severely shock loaded or damaged. Rigging should follow ANSI Z133 and be run by trained crew members.

faq.q: Do I need 3/4 inch rope for most tree jobs?
faq.a: Usually not. Many crews use smaller rope day to day and keep 3/4 inch for heavy removal rigging.

faq.q: What hardware works with 3/4 inch rigging line?
faq.a: Use blocks, lowering devices, and slings rated for 3/4 inch rope. Check each maker's specified rope range.

name: Marlow Raptor 14mm Rigging Rope
title: Marlow Raptor 14mm Rigging Rope for Arborists
meta: Marlow Raptor 14mm rigging rope is a mid-size line for everyday tree rigging. Where it fits, what hardware to pair it with, and how to inspect and retire it.
tagline: A 14mm Marlow rigging line for everyday pruning and removal rigging.
summary: Marlow Raptor 14mm rigging rope is a mid-size rigging line from a long-established British rope maker, sized for everyday removal and pruning rigging. At about 9/16 inch it suits most standard rigging blocks and lowering devices crews already own.
highlights: Fits common blocks and lowering devices
From a well-known UK rope maker
specs: See the maker's rated breaking strength

p: A 14mm rigging line covers a lot of daily work: lowering limbs on pruning jobs, negative rigging small to mid-size tops, and speed-lining brush to the drop zone. It is lighter and easier to handle than a 16 or 18mm line, so it gets used rather than left on the truck.
For big wood, step up to a heavier line such as the 18mm Raptor. See all our rigging rope options to build a set that covers your jobs.

A mid-size line also makes a good second rope on bigger jobs, used as a tag line or for small pieces while the heavy line handles the main rigging. Having two rigging lines set up keeps the climber cutting while the ground crew clears.

Check the rope range on your block, porta-wrap, and slings, and use the maker's rated strength with a working load limit that allows for shock loading. Knots, sharp bends, and edges all cut into strength.

Inspect before every job for cut strands, glazing from friction, stiff or flat sections, and core damage. Keep it clean and away from fuel and bar oil. Rigging operations should follow ANSI Z133 and be run by trained crew.
Keep a simple log of each rope's age, use, and any big shock loads so the crew knows when it is due for retirement.

faq.q: Is 14mm rope strong enough for removals?
faq.a: It suits many small to mid-size removals. For heavy blocking, use a larger line and rated hardware.

faq.q: Can I splice Marlow Raptor?
faq.a: Follow the maker's splicing guidance for this construction, or have a qualified splicer do it.

name: Marlow Raptor 18mm Rigging Rope
title: Marlow Raptor 18mm Rigging Rope for Heavy Rigging
meta: Marlow Raptor 18mm rigging rope is a heavier line for big removals and blocking down wood. How it compares with 14mm, what hardware it needs, and checks.
tagline: A heavier 18mm Marlow rigging line for big removals and blocking down wood.
summary: Marlow Raptor 18mm rigging rope is the heavier line in the Raptor family, sized for removals where you block down large wood and want more strength margin. At about 3/4 inch it calls for full-size rigging blocks and lowering devices rated for that diameter.
highlights: Strong grip on the lowering side
specs: See the maker's rated breaking strength

p: When the wood gets big, shock loads climb fast. An 18mm line gives you more strength and more material to wear before it is compromised, which is why crews reserve a heavy line for blocking down trunks and large leaders.
It weighs more and takes up more room, so most crews pair it with a lighter line like the 14mm Raptor for daily work. Compare the full range in our rigging rope section.

Heavier rope also gives the ground worker more to hold. With a few wraps on a porta-wrap or bollard, an 18mm line lets the ground crew let the run of the rope absorb energy and bring a big piece to a stop more gently than a skinny line would.

Use blocks, porta-wraps, and slings that list 18mm or 3/4 inch rope in their range. Set a working load limit from the maker's rated strength with room for shock, and remember knots and tight bends reduce strength.

Before every job, check for cut strands, glazing, flat or stiff spots, and core damage, and retire any rope that has taken a severe shock load. Heavy rigging should follow ANSI Z133 and be planned by a qualified crew leader.
Store it coiled loosely or flaked in a bag, out of sun and away from fuel and chemicals, and keep a record of the jobs it has done.

faq.q: Should I buy the 14mm or 18mm Raptor?
faq.a: Many crews own both: 14mm for daily rigging and 18mm for heavy removals. Choose by the size of wood you regularly block down.

faq.q: Will 18mm rope fit my rigging block?
faq.a: Check the block's marked rope range. Many full-size blocks take 3/4 inch rope, but smaller blocks may not.

name: Teufelberger Sta-Set Rigging Rope 5/8"
title: Teufelberger Sta-Set Rigging Rope, 5/8 Inch
meta: Sta-Set rigging rope in 5/8 inch is a polyester double braid for rigging, tag lines, and pulling. What it does well, hardware fit, and inspection advice.
tagline: A 5/8 inch polyester double braid line for rigging, tag lines, and pulling.
summary: Sta-Set rigging rope is a polyester double braid line from New England Ropes, now part of Teufelberger, and the 5/8 inch size is a common choice for general rigging and pulling work. It holds its shape, runs smoothly through hardware, and resists abrasion well.
highlights: Firm, round, and easy to handle

p: Sta-Set has been around a long time and shows up in many applications, from marine work to tree crews. A polyester double braid stays firm and round, which helps it run through blocks and lowering devices without flattening, and it holds up to the dirt and bark of daily rigging.
In 5/8 inch it works for lowering limbs, rigging moderate tops, and as a pull line for directional felling. For lighter or heavier work, compare other lines in our rigging rope.
Low stretch is the other reason crews like it. When you are pulling a tree over with a 3:1 or snugging a tag line, a rope that does not stretch much means less wasted pull and more direct control.

Double braid can be spliced with standard double braid techniques for eyes on slings and rigging lines. Match the rope to the rope range of your block, wrap device, and slings, and work from the maker's rated strength with a working load limit that allows for shock.

Inspect before every use for cut or pulled strands, glazed areas, core showing through the cover, or lumps that suggest internal damage. Keep it out of fuel and bar oil. Rigging should follow ANSI Z133 and be done by trained crew.

faq.q: Is Sta-Set the same as a dedicated arborist rigging rope?
faq.a: It is a general-purpose polyester double braid that many arborists use for rigging and pulling. Dedicated arborist lines may handle differently, so pick by feel and job.

faq.q: Can I splice 5/8 Sta-Set?
faq.a: Yes, it takes standard double braid splices. Have a trained splicer do it for rigging use.

name: CMI 1" Arborist Rigging Block
title: CMI Arborist Rigging Block for 1 Inch Rope
meta: The CMI arborist rigging block in the 1 inch size takes big rope for heavy blocking on removals. How to hang it, match the rope, and inspect it before each job.
tagline: A heavy-duty CMI rigging block for large rope and big removal work.
summary: The CMI arborist rigging block in the 1 inch size is a full-size block for heavy removal rigging, made to accept rope up to the large diameters crews use for blocking down big wood. It hangs from a sling at the rigging point and gives the lowering line a smooth, strong path.
highlights: Sized for rope up to 1 inch
For heavy removals and blocking down
Made by a US rope-hardware maker
specs: Up to 1 in, per model name

p: A rigging block takes the lowering line through a strong, large sheave at the rigging point so the load comes down under control and friction is managed at the porta-wrap instead of on the tree. A 1 inch block is made for heavy rigging where crews run big rope and block down large wood.
Hang it with a sling rated for the job, high and close to the stem, and keep the line running straight into the sheave. Compare sizes in our rigging blocks before choosing.

A block also protects the rope. Running a heavy lowering line over a bare crotch burns the bark and the rope, while a sheave lets the line move cleanly and puts the friction where the ground worker can control it.

Read the block's marked rating and remember the force on a rigging point can be close to double the load on the line when the rope runs back down the tree. Plan with that in mind and use slings, rope, and lowering devices that match.

Before each job, check the sheave for smooth spin and wear grooves, the side plates for cracks or bends, and the axle and bushings for play. Retire the block if it has taken a severe shock load. Rigging should follow ANSI Z133.
Keep a record of the block's service history, especially any big shock loads, so the crew knows its condition.

faq.q: Can I run smaller rope through a 1 inch block?
faq.a: Usually yes, within the marked rope range. Smaller rope may not sit as well in the sheave groove, so check with the maker.

faq.q: How should I attach the block?
faq.a: Use a rated rigging sling, choked or girth-hitched high on the stem as the maker and your training direct.

name: CMI 3/4" Aluminum Rigging Block
title: CMI Aluminum Rigging Block for 3/4 Inch Rope
meta: The CMI aluminum rigging block in the 3/4 inch size is a lighter block for removal rigging. How it compares with a 1 inch block, how to hang it, and checks.
tagline: A lighter aluminum CMI block for everyday removal rigging up to 3/4 inch rope.
summary: The CMI aluminum rigging block in the 3/4 inch size is a full-function rigging block built lighter, for crews who rig often and want less weight to haul up the tree. It takes the common rigging rope sizes up to 3/4 inch.
highlights: Smooth path for the lowering line
specs: Up to 3/4 in, per model name

p: Every pound counts when you are carrying gear aloft and setting rigging points all day. An aluminum block gives you a proper rigging block, with a large sheave and a strong frame, at a weight that makes it easier to send up and reposition.
The 3/4 inch size covers the rope most crews use for daily rigging. For the biggest wood, a 1 inch block may be the better tool. See all our rigging blocks to compare.

A lighter block also makes it easier to reposition the rigging point as the removal comes down. Rather than leaving a heavy block where it is and rigging from a poor angle, the climber can move it to a better spot quickly.

Use the marked rating and remember the rigging point load can be close to twice the load on the line. Pair the block with slings, rope, and a lowering device in the same range, and keep the line running straight into the sheave.

Aluminum shows wear faster than steel, so inspect the sheave groove for grooving, the side plates for cracks, burrs, or bending, and the axle for play before each job. Retire the block after a severe shock load. Follow ANSI Z133 for all rigging.

faq.q: Is an aluminum block strong enough for removals?
faq.a: Within its marked rating, yes. Choose the size and rating for the loads you expect to generate.

faq.q: What rope should I use with it?
faq.a: Rope within the marked range, up to 3/4 inch. Match the sling and lowering device as well.

name: ISC Compact Rigging Pulley (Grey with Grey Wheel)
title: ISC Compact Rigging Pulley for Light Removal Rigging
meta: The ISC compact rigging pulley is a small rigging block for pruning and light removal work. Where it fits, how it compares with larger blocks, and checks.
tagline: A small ISC rigging pulley for pruning and light removal rigging.
summary: The ISC compact rigging pulley is a small rigging block for pruning and light removal work, where a full-size block is more than you need. This version has a grey frame and a grey sheave, and it hangs from a sling at the rigging point like a larger block.
highlights: Lighter to carry than a full-size block

p: Plenty of rigging is not heavy rigging: lowering limbs over a roof on a pruning job, taking small tops in pieces, or controlling brush over a fence. A compact rigging pulley handles these jobs with less weight than a full-size block, so you are more likely to rig the piece than to drop it and hope.
Step up to a medium or large block when the wood gets bigger. Compare sizes in our rigging blocks.

A compact block is light enough to send up with the climber at the start of the job and leave on the saddle until needed. That makes it easier to rig a limb over a target rather than take the chance of a free drop.

Check the marked rope range and rating, and remember the rigging point sees close to double the line load. Keep shock loads modest by limiting drop distance and letting the ground worker run the friction smoothly.

Before each use, spin the sheave, check the side plates and frame for cracks or bends, and look for grooves in the sheave. Clean off sap and grit. Rigging should follow ANSI Z133 and the maker's instructions.
Store it clean and dry, and retire it if it has been shock loaded beyond its rating or dropped onto a hard surface from height.

faq.q: Can the ISC compact pulley replace my main rigging block?
faq.a: For light work, yes. For blocking down big wood, use a larger block rated for the loads.

faq.q: Does the color mean anything?
faq.a: The grey frame and grey wheel identify this version. Check the marking for its rope range and rating.

name: ISC Medium Rigging Pulley for 20mm Rope (Grey with Green Wheel)
title: ISC Medium Rigging Pulley for 20mm Rope
h1: ISC Medium Rigging Pulley for 20mm Rope
meta: The ISC medium rigging pulley takes rope up to 20mm for heavier removal rigging. How it compares with the compact pulley, how to hang it, and how to inspect it.
tagline: A mid-size ISC rigging block for heavier removals with rope up to 20mm.
summary: The ISC medium rigging pulley is a mid-size rigging block made for rope up to 20mm, which covers the heavier lines crews use on removals. This version has a grey frame and a green sheave, and it fills the gap between compact pulleys and the largest blocks.

p: When you are rigging tops and leaders on a removal, you need a block that can take a heavier line and the shock that comes with blocking wood. The medium ISC rigging pulley takes rope up to 20mm, so it works with the 5/8 and 3/4 inch class lines many crews run for removals.
It is heavier than a compact pulley, but far more appropriate for big pieces. Compare it with other rigging blocks to find the right size for your work.

Because the frame is built for a heavier line, it also tolerates the wear of daily removal work better than smaller pulleys. Pair it with a rigging sling and lowering device rated for the same rope and load range.
Read the marked rating on the pulley before use and plan for the rigging point to see close to double the line load. Match the sling, rope, and lowering device to the same working range.

Inspect the sheave, side plates, and axle before every job, looking for cracks, bends, grooves, and play. Retire the pulley after a severe shock load or any damage you cannot rule out. Rigging should follow ANSI Z133 and the maker's instructions.
Store it clean and dry and keep a simple record of the jobs it has done.

faq.q: What rope sizes can I use in the ISC medium pulley?
faq.a: Rope up to 20mm. Check the marking and the maker's documentation for the full range.

faq.q: Medium or compact ISC pulley?
faq.a: Compact suits pruning and light work. Medium suits removals and heavier lines up to 20mm.

name: SMC Apex Direct 1.5 Pulley
title: SMC Apex Direct 1.5 Pulley for Rigging and Haul Systems
meta: The SMC Apex Direct 1.5 is a larger rescue-grade pulley for haul systems, redirects, and light rigging. How tree crews use it, sizing notes, and inspection.
tagline: A larger SMC rescue-grade pulley for haul systems and light rigging.
summary: The SMC Apex Direct 1.5 is a rescue-grade pulley in a larger size than the 1.1 version, giving a bigger sheave for haul systems, redirects, and light rigging. Tree crews use it where a micro pulley is too small but a full rigging block is more than the job needs.
highlights: Larger size in the SMC Apex Direct line

p: A bigger sheave bends the rope less and generally runs more efficiently, which you feel when you are pulling through a 3:1 to tension a line, hauling a heavy tool to the climber, or redirecting a lowering line around a stem.
The 1.5 size sits between compact pulleys and true rigging blocks. Compare it with the 1.1 and other options in our rigging blocks to match the pulley to your system.
It also suits tag lines that have to run around a stem or over a fence. The larger sheave reduces wear on the rope and makes the ground worker's job easier.
Read the side-plate markings for the rope range and strength and keep loads well inside them. Do not use it in place of a rigging block for blocking down heavy wood.

Before each use, spin the sheave, check the side plates and axle for cracks, burrs, or play, and clean off sap and grit. If it goes into a climbing or rescue system, life-support use must follow ANSI Z133, the manufacturer's instructions, and your training.
Store it dry and away from chemicals, and retire it after a drop from height onto a hard surface unless the maker says otherwise.

faq.q: Should I choose the 1.1 or the 1.5 size?
faq.a: The 1.1 is lighter and more compact. The 1.5 gives a larger sheave for smoother running in haul systems.

faq.q: Can it replace a rigging block?
faq.a: Not for heavy or shock-loaded rigging. Use a rated rigging block for blocking down wood.

name: Rock Exotica TriRig
title: Rock Exotica TriRig: Rigging Plate for Rope Systems
meta: The Rock Exotica TriRig is a compact rigging plate for organizing anchors, pulleys, and carabiners in rope systems. How crews use it and how to inspect it.
tagline: A compact rigging plate for organizing anchors and connectors in rope systems.
summary: The Rock Exotica TriRig is a compact rigging plate that gives a rope system several connection points in one piece of hardware. Tree crews use a plate like this to organize an anchor, keep carabiners from cross-loading, and build tidy haul or lowering systems.
highlights: Multiple connection points in one plate
Keeps carabiners organized and loaded correctly
Useful for anchors and haul systems

p: When several pieces meet at one anchor, carabiners stacked on carabiners can twist, cross-load, and turn a simple setup into a tangle. A rigging plate gives each piece its own hole: the anchor sling on one side, the pulley or lowering device on another, a backup or tag line on a third.

On tree jobs that might mean a ground anchor for a 3:1, a rescue or haul setup, or a neat way to split a load between two slings. Browse more blocks and rigging hardware to build the rest of the system.

Load the plate in line with the direction the maker shows, use correctly sized carabiners, and keep everything inside the marked rating. Spread angles between anchor legs increase the force on each leg, so keep them narrow.

Check for cracks, burrs, deformation, and worn edges in the holes before each use. Retire the plate if it has been dropped from height onto a hard surface or shock loaded. If it is part of a life-support system, life-support use must follow ANSI Z133, the manufacturer's instructions, and your training.
Store it with your other rigging hardware, away from chemicals, and keep it clean so you can see any damage at a glance.

faq.q: Do I need a rigging plate for tree work?
faq.a: Not always, but it makes multi-piece anchors and haul systems cleaner and helps prevent cross-loaded carabiners.

faq.q: Can I use the TriRig in a climbing system?
faq.a: Check the maker's rating and instructions. Use life-support gear only as the manufacturer and ANSI Z133 allow.

name: Petzl SPIN L2 Pulley
title: Petzl SPIN L2 Double Pulley with Swivel
meta: The Petzl SPIN L2 is a double pulley with a built-in swivel for haul systems and rigging. How tree crews use it, why the swivel helps, and care tips.
tagline: A swiveling double pulley for haul systems, redirects, and rope work.
summary: The Petzl SPIN L2 is a double pulley with a built-in swivel and sealed ball-bearing sheaves, made for haul systems and rope work where efficiency matters. Tree crews use it to build mechanical advantage for tensioning lines, pulling tops, and lifting gear.
highlights: Built-in swivel keeps ropes from twisting
Opens to load the rope with the pulley clipped in
Good base for haul and tensioning systems

body.h: Why a double pulley with a swivel
p: A double pulley lets you build higher ratios, such as a 4:1 or 5:1, with fewer parts. The integrated swivel lets the pulley turn to line up with the load, so the rope strands do not twist around each other as you haul. That matters when you are pulling a lean out of a tree or tensioning a speed line across a yard.
Petzl's side plates open so you can load the rope without unclipping the pulley from its anchor. See our other rigging pulleys for single options to pair it with.
Sealed ball bearings keep friction low, so more of your pull goes into the load. That matters on long hauls or when you are building a high ratio system.

Check the marked rope range and rating and stay well within them. Mechanical advantage multiplies your pull, which makes it easy to overload a sling, an anchor, or a tree, so plan the forces before you start.

Before each use, spin both sheaves, test the swivel, and check the side plates for cracks or deformation. Rinse off grit and sap and let it dry. If it becomes part of a rescue or life-support system, life-support use must follow ANSI Z133, the manufacturer's instructions, and your training.

faq.q: What is the difference between the SPIN L1 and SPIN L2?
faq.a: The SPIN L1 is a single pulley, and the SPIN L2 is a double. Both have a swivel and ball-bearing sheaves.

faq.q: Can I use the SPIN L2 for blocking down wood?
faq.a: No. It is a haul and tensioning pulley. Use a rated rigging block for shock-loaded rigging.

name: Progress Capture Pulley 40kN, Double Bushing
title: Progress Capture Pulley 40kN with Double Bushing
meta: A 40kN progress capture pulley with double bushings, made to work with a prusik in haul systems. How progress capture works and how to inspect it before use.
tagline: A pulley shaped to tend a prusik, so a haul system holds every pull.
summary: A progress capture pulley is a pulley with square-edged side plates that let a prusik or friction hitch sit against it without being pulled into the sheave. This one carries a 40kN rating and uses double bushings, and crews use it to build haul systems that hold their gain between pulls.
highlights: Side plates shaped to tend a prusik
Builds haul systems that hold their gain

p: In a haul system you pull, then you have to reset. Without something to hold the rope, you lose what you just gained. A progress capture pulley works with a prusik on the line: as you pull, rope runs through the pulley and the prusik slides against the side plates. When you let go, the prusik grabs and the load stays put.
On tree jobs that might mean pulling a top over in a felling setup, tensioning a speed line, or lifting a heavy piece off a structure. Find more options in our rigging pulleys.

The square-edged side plates are what make it work. A rounded pulley can drag the prusik into the sheave, where it fails to grab, while a progress capture pulley stops the hitch at the side plates every time.

Bushings are simple and durable and handle high static loads, though they spin with more friction than ball bearings. Keep loads within the rating and remember mechanical advantage makes it easy to overload anchors and trees.

Check the sheave, side plates, and axle for wear, cracks, and play before each use, and inspect the prusik for glazing. Rescue and life-support use must follow the manufacturer's instructions, ANSI Z133, and proper training.
Store it clean and dry, and keep it with the prusiks you use with it so the system is complete when you need it.

faq.q: What is the difference between bushings and ball bearings?
faq.a: Bushings are durable and simple but have more friction. Ball bearings spin more freely and suit long hauls.

faq.q: Can I use a standard pulley with a prusik?
faq.a: Only if it is designed to tend a prusik. Rounded side plates can pull the hitch into the sheave.

name: Rock Exotica Omni-Block 1.1
title: Rock Exotica Omni-Block 1.1 Swivel Pulley
meta: The Rock Exotica Omni-Block 1.1 is a swivel pulley that opens with the carabiner still in place. How tree crews use it for redirects, haul systems, and climbs.
tagline: A swiveling Rock Exotica pulley that loads rope without unclipping.
summary: The Rock Exotica Omni-Block 1.1 is a compact swivel pulley whose side plates open while it stays clipped to the anchor, so you can load the rope without dropping anything. Tree climbers and rigging crews use it for redirects, haul systems, and climbing system setups.
highlights: Side plates open while still clipped
Redirects, haul systems, and climbing setups

p: Being able to open a pulley without unclipping it is a real advantage aloft. You can drop the rope in mid-system, keep the pulley attached to the anchor, and avoid fumbling hardware over a drop zone. The swivel lets the pulley line up with the load so ropes do not twist.
Climbers use it in SRT base anchors, redirects, and haul systems, and rigging crews use it for tag lines and light tensioning. Compare it with other rigging pulleys.
The rounded frame and smooth sheave keep friction low, so it works well in haul systems and anywhere a rope needs to change direction without much wear.
Read the marked rope range and rating and keep loads inside them. It is not a rigging block for blocking down wood.

Before each use, check that the side plates close and lock fully, the swivel turns freely, and the sheave spins smoothly with no grooves or play. Rinse off grit and sap. Life-support use must follow the maker's instructions, ANSI Z133, and your training.
Store it clean and dry, away from chemicals, and retire it after a drop from height onto a hard surface unless the maker says otherwise.

faq.q: Can I use the Omni-Block in my climbing system?
faq.a: Many climbers do. Confirm it meets your system's requirements and use it per the maker's instructions and ANSI Z133.

faq.q: What does the 1.1 mean?
faq.a: It is the size designation in the Omni-Block range. Larger sizes are made for bigger rope and loads.

name: Petzl SPIN L1D Pulley
title: Petzl SPIN L1D Swivel Pulley with Becket
meta: The Petzl SPIN L1D is a swivel pulley with a becket for building haul systems and tensioning lines. How tree crews use it, what the becket adds, and checks.
tagline: A swivel pulley with a becket for building compact haul systems.
summary: The Petzl SPIN L1D is a single swivel pulley with a becket, an extra attachment point below the sheave, and sealed ball-bearing efficiency. Tree crews use it to build compact haul systems, tension speed lines, and redirect ropes with low friction.
highlights: Becket attachment point for haul systems

p: A becket is an extra attachment point on the pulley. It lets you tie or clip the end of the rope directly to the pulley, which is how you build a compact 3:1 or 5:1 with fewer carabiners. The swivel keeps strands from twisting as you haul.
On tree jobs that might be a quick system to tension a speed line, pull a lean out of a tree, or lift a stuck saw. Pair it with the SPIN L2 and other rigging pulleys for higher ratios.
Because the side plates open while the pulley stays clipped, you can load the rope in mid-system without dropping anything over the work zone.
Stay inside the marked rope range and rating and plan forces before you pull, because mechanical advantage makes overloading easy.

Before each use, spin the sheave, check the swivel and becket for wear or deformation, and confirm the side plates close fully. Rinse and dry it after dirty jobs. Life-support use must follow the maker's instructions, ANSI Z133, and your training.
Retire it after a drop from height onto a hard surface unless Petzl's guidance says otherwise, and keep a record of its use.

faq.q: SPIN L1 or SPIN L1D?
faq.a: The L1D adds a becket, an extra attachment point, which is handy for building haul systems.

faq.q: Is it suitable for blocking down wood?
faq.a: No. Use a rated rigging block for shock-loaded rigging.

name: ISC Rigging Rope Wrench (70kg)
title: ISC Rigging Rope Wrench for Light Lowering
meta: The ISC rigging rope wrench adds friction for lowering light loads up to 70kg. Where it fits on pruning jobs, how it differs from a porta-wrap, and checks.
tagline: A friction device for lowering light limbs and brush in the canopy.
summary: The ISC rigging rope wrench is a friction device for lowering light loads, listed for up to 70kg, that crews use when a porta-wrap at the base is more than the job needs. It helps a climber or ground worker control small limbs and brush on pruning jobs.
highlights: Good for pruning and small limbs
From ISC, maker of the original Rope Wrench
specs: Up to 70 kg, per product name

p: Plenty of pruning cuts are too heavy to drop over a roof or a garden but nowhere near the size that needs a full rigging block and porta-wrap. A light-duty rope wrench adds just enough friction to let a limb down slowly and in control.
It works with smaller rope and lighter loads than heavy lowering devices, so it is quick to set and easy to carry. See our other lowering devices when the wood gets bigger.
Unlike a porta-wrap at the base of the tree, a light device like this can be set close to the work, which suits single-person pruning setups where the climber controls the descent of small limbs.
The 70kg figure is a hard limit, not a guide. Shock loading a light device by letting pieces free-fall onto it multiplies the force, so keep pieces small and catch them with little slack.

Follow ISC's instructions for rope size, setup, and inspection. Check for wear grooves, cracks, and burrs before each use. Do not use it as a climbing device unless the maker says it is designed for that. Rigging should follow ANSI Z133 and be done by trained crew.
Store it clean and dry, and keep it with the rope it was set up for so the system stays matched.

faq.q: Is the ISC rigging rope wrench the same as the climbing Rope Wrench?
faq.a: No. This version is for rigging light loads. Use climbing devices only as their maker intends.

faq.q: What happens if I exceed 70kg?
faq.a: You risk losing control of the load and damaging the device. Use a heavier lowering device for larger pieces.

name: CMI RopeJack Bag
title: CMI RopeJack Bag for Storing Rigging Gear
meta: The CMI RopeJack bag keeps a RopeJack or mechanical advantage kit together and protected in the truck. What it holds, why a dedicated bag helps, and care tips.
tagline: A dedicated bag to keep a RopeJack or haul kit together and protected.
summary: The CMI RopeJack bag is a dedicated carry bag for CMI's RopeJack and its accessories, so a mechanical advantage kit stays together and protected in the truck box. When the tree needs a pull, the whole kit comes out in one grab.
highlights: Dedicated bag for the CMI RopeJack
Protects hardware from grit and weather
Easy to grab from the truck

p: A mechanical advantage kit is only useful if all the parts are there when you need them. Keeping the RopeJack, its carabiners, and slings in their own bag means the kit comes out complete, every time, rather than pieces drifting into other bags on the truck.
A bag also keeps grit and moisture off the hardware. Browse our mechanical advantage section for gear to round out the kit.
When the pull needs to happen fast, such as a tree that sits back on the saw, nobody wants to search the truck for a missing carabiner. A dedicated bag keeps the kit ready.
Pack the hardware so it does not rattle or rub against sharp edges, and keep the bag away from fuel, bar oil, and chemicals. Let wet gear dry before you pack it away.
Use the time when you pack the bag to inspect the kit: check slings for cuts and the hardware for cracks or burrs. The bag itself is storage only and is not a load-bearing item.

Check the bag itself for torn seams, worn bottoms, and broken zippers or closures, and replace it before it starts losing gear. A clear label on the outside helps the crew grab the right bag on a busy job.

faq.q: Does the bag come with a RopeJack?
faq.a: No. This is the bag only. Check the listing for what is included.

faq.q: Can I store other gear in it?
faq.a: Yes, it works for any small rigging or haul kit that fits.

name: Petzl JAG TRAXION Double Pulley
title: Petzl JAG TRAXION Progress Capture Double Pulley
meta: The Petzl JAG TRAXION is a double pulley with built-in progress capture for compact haul systems. How tree crews use it, setting up a 4:1, and inspection.
tagline: A double pulley with built-in progress capture for compact haul systems.
summary: The Petzl JAG TRAXION is a double pulley with built-in progress capture, so a haul system holds the load each time you stop pulling. It is the heart of Petzl's JAG system kits, and tree crews use it to tension lines and pull tops with a compact, efficient 4:1.
highlights: Core of a compact 4:1 haul system

p: Pair the JAG TRAXION with a second double pulley and you have a compact 4:1 that grabs and holds every pull. That makes it handy for tensioning a speed line, pulling a lean out of a tree before the cut, or lifting a stuck piece off a structure. Because it holds on its own, you can reset without needing a second person on a prusik.
See our other mechanical advantage gear for kits and accessories.
Efficient ball-bearing sheaves mean less of your pull is lost to friction, which matters when you need to move something heavy with a small crew.
Mechanical advantage makes it easy to exceed what an anchor, sling, or tree can handle, so plan the forces before you pull and stay well inside the marked rating.

Before each use, check the cam for free movement and clean teeth, spin the sheaves, and look for cracks, wear, or deformation. Rinse off grit and sap. Rescue and life-support use must follow the maker's instructions, ANSI Z133, and proper training.
Store it dry and away from chemicals, and retire it after a drop from height or any damage you cannot rule out.

faq.q: Can I use the JAG TRAXION alone?
faq.a: It works best as part of a system with a second pulley. Petzl sells complete JAG system kits.

faq.q: Does the cam damage rope?
faq.a: Used correctly, no. Avoid shock loading it and keep the cam clean.

name: 1/2" Soft Anchor Ring Sling with Medium Ring
title: 1/2 Inch Ring Sling with Medium Ring for Rigging
h1: 1/2" Soft Anchor Ring Sling with Medium Ring
meta: A 1/2 inch ring sling with a medium ring gives an adjustable rigging point that sets in seconds. How a ring sling works, sizing tips, and inspection advice.
tagline: An adjustable rope sling with a medium ring for quick rigging points.
summary: A ring sling with a medium ring is an adjustable rope sling that lets you set a rigging point at any height and wrap it to the stem in seconds. This version uses 1/2 inch rope and a medium ring, a common combination for everyday rigging.
highlights: Medium ring for an adjustable anchor
Sets quickly on most stem sizes
Rope is softer on bark than chain

p: A fixed-length sling either fits the stem or it does not. A ring sling lets you wrap the stem, pass the tail through the ring, and adjust until the block sits exactly where you want it. It sets quickly, holds well, and comes down easily when the job moves on.
Use it for rigging points, block anchors, and as a choker for natural crotch rigging. Find more in our adjustable slings.
Because it adjusts, one ring sling can cover a wide range of stem sizes. That means fewer slings to carry up the tree and less time spent swapping slings when the first one does not fit.
Read the tag for the rated strength and keep working loads well below it. A choked hitch reduces strength, and a rigging point under a running line can see close to double the load.
Check the rope for cuts, glazing, and flat spots, and the ring for cracks, burrs, or wear grooves before each use. Retire the sling if the tag is missing. Rigging should follow ANSI Z133.
Store it dry and away from fuel and chemicals, and keep a record of its use, especially any big shock loads.

faq.q: Can I use a ring sling as a rigging block anchor?
faq.a: Yes, that is one of its main uses. Make sure its rating suits the forces involved.

faq.q: Why choose a medium ring?
faq.a: It passes 1/2 inch rope cleanly while staying compact. Larger rings suit bigger rope.

name: 1/2" x 4' Tenex Soft Anchor Rigging Sling
title: Tenex Soft Anchor Rigging Sling, 1/2 Inch x 4 Foot
h1: 1/2" x 4' Tenex Soft Anchor Rigging Sling
meta: A 1/2 inch by 4 foot Tenex soft anchor rigging sling for rigging points and anchors. Why Tenex suits slings, sizing advice, and inspection tips for crews.
tagline: A 4 foot Tenex soft anchor sling for rigging points and anchors.
summary: This 1/2 inch by 4 foot Tenex soft anchor rigging sling is built from Samson's Tenex single braid polyester, which splices easily and holds up to abrasion. Crews use it to set rigging points, anchor blocks, and build soft anchors on stems.

p: Tenex is a 12 strand single braid polyester rope from Samson. It splices cleanly into strong eyes, it is firm enough to hold its shape, and polyester resists abrasion and holds up to sun and weather. Those traits make it a common choice for rigging and anchor slings.
At 4 feet, this sling suits small and mid-size stems for rigging points and soft anchors. Look through our adjustable slings for other lengths.
Soft slings are also kinder to the tree you are leaving behind than chain or wire, and they are lighter to carry aloft. A short sling like this lives easily on the saddle or in the rigging bag.
Read the tag for its rated strength and remember a choker or girth hitch reduces it. A rigging point can see close to double the line load when the line runs back to the ground.

Inspect before each use for cuts, glazing, flat spots, and pulled strands, and check the splices for slipping. Retire the sling if the tag is gone or it has been severely shock loaded. Rigging should follow ANSI Z133.
Store it dry and away from fuel and chemicals, and keep a record of its use.

faq.q: Is Tenex the same as double braid?
faq.a: No. Tenex is a 12 strand single braid, which splices more easily than double braid.

faq.q: Is a 4 foot sling long enough?
faq.a: It suits small and mid-size stems. Choose longer slings for larger stems.

name: Tylaska DTR20 Arborist Rigging Ring
title: Tylaska DTR20 Arborist Rigging Ring
meta: The Tylaska DTR20 arborist rigging ring is a machined low-friction ring for rigging points and redirects. How crews use rigging rings and what to check.
tagline: A machined Tylaska ring for low-friction rigging points and redirects.
summary: The Tylaska DTR20 arborist rigging ring is a machined ring from a maker known for marine and rigging hardware, used by tree crews as a low-friction rigging point or redirect. Rope runs smoothly over its rounded profile, with no moving parts to wear out.

p: A rigging ring sits in a sling at the rigging point and gives the line a smooth, rounded surface to run over. It is simpler than a block, with no sheave or bearings, and it adds a bit of friction that can help a ground worker control lighter loads.
Crews also use rings as redirects and as connection points in soft anchors. Browse our rings and rigging hardware for related gear.
Because there are no moving parts, a ring is simple to set and hard to break. It lives easily on the saddle or in a sling, and it is a good choice for jobs where a block would be more than you need.
Check the maker's rating and rope range and keep loads well within them. A rigging point can see close to double the line load, so plan for it.
Before each use, look for grooves worn by the rope, cracks, sharp edges, and deformation. Retire the ring if it has taken a severe shock load. Rigging should follow ANSI Z133.
Store it clean and dry, and retire it after a drop from height onto a hard surface unless the maker says otherwise.

faq.q: Ring or block for rigging?
faq.a: A ring is simpler and adds friction. A block has less friction and suits heavier, faster loads.

faq.q: Can the DTR20 be used for climbing?
faq.a: Check Tylaska's documentation. Use life-support gear only as the manufacturer and ANSI Z133 allow.

name: Climbing Technology Steel Ring
title: Climbing Technology Steel Ring for Arborist Use
meta: The Climbing Technology steel ring is a durable ring for friction savers, anchors, and redirects. Where steel beats aluminum and how to inspect it before use.
tagline: A durable steel ring for friction savers, anchors, and redirects.
summary: The Climbing Technology steel ring is a durable connection ring that arborists use in friction savers, anchors, and redirects. Steel holds up to rope wear better than aluminum, which matters for gear that sees rope running over it all day.

p: Rings show up all over a climbing setup: the ends of a friction saver, anchor points, and redirects. When rope runs over a ring repeatedly, aluminum wears grooves faster. Steel lasts longer and handles abrasion better, at the cost of a little extra weight.
Compare it with other climbing rings to choose size and material.

On a friction saver, the ring takes rope wear every time you advance or descend. A steel ring lasts much longer under that kind of use, and it is less likely to develop the sharp grooves that can damage your climbing line.
Steel rings also work as anchor points for redirects and as connection points in rigging setups where you want a simple, durable piece of hardware that will not wear out quickly.
Check the rating and the maker's instructions before putting the ring into service. Use it only in configurations the maker approves.

Before each climb, look for grooves, cracks, rust pitting, and sharp edges, and retire the ring if you find any. Life-support use must follow ANSI Z133, the manufacturer's instructions, and your training.
Store it dry to prevent rust, and keep it away from chemicals. Wipe it down after wet or sappy climbs, and do not apply oils or coatings unless the maker approves them for use with rope.

faq.q: Steel or aluminum ring?
faq.a: Steel wears longer and resists abrasion. Aluminum is lighter. Choose by how much rope runs over the ring.

faq.q: Can I use this ring in a climbing system?
faq.a: Check the rating and maker's instructions. Life-support use must meet ANSI Z133 and be inspected.
